The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and proc

sociated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.

entity_geography.text: dio Reading Download (BARD) Wishlist, stream NLS talking books, and manage the patron’s Bookshelf using a voice-only interface available on Alexa-enabled commercial smart-speaker platforms. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. C.2 BACKGROUND NLS administers a free program that loans audio and braille books and magazines, music scores in braille and large print, and specially designed audio-playback and refreshable-braille-display equipment to residents of the United States who are unable to read or use standard print materials due to visual or physical impairment. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. This service is also extended to eligible American citizens residing abroad. Therefore, Crestron remains the only provider capable of meeting the technical and compatibility needs for this upgrade. 2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used? Include any dollar, schedule, or compatibility impacts if possible. Utilizing a different vendor or brand could result in significant schedule delays, as the government would need to evaluate, integrate, and train personnel on unfamiliar equipment. e medical capabilities, austere mission environments, field hospitals and Forward Operating Bases. DoW’s close relationship with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is paramount. The success of an integrated Federal Electronic Health Record (EHR) is a top national priority. Equally critical is the ability to support the continuum of care across operational and enterprise healthcare environments, ensuring that health information generated during military operations can be captured, exchanged, and made available to support continued care within the enterprise health record. Together, these operational, enterprise, and interagency requirements create a highly complex healthcare ecosystem that includes deployed medical environments, fixed medical treatment facilities, the Federal Health Care Center and other DoW/VA sharing sites. Supporting the ecosystem requires coordinated end user service models and highly configurable enterprise approaches capable of operating across diverse mission environments while enabling interoperability, continuity of care, and interagency collaboration. 1.2 EUS Overview & Transition Strategy To maximize the value of the Department’s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unifie

le DDIL Operations: Ensure training, adoption, and communication resources are available offline and locally to support operational units in Denied, Disrupted, Intermittent, and Limited (DDIL) environments. Maintain a deployable surge capacity to provide short-notice, onsite tactical training, workflow support, and physical setup/teardown of training hardware during military exercises. • Parallel Innovation Framework: Establish a low-risk framework to test, scale, and deploy automated workflows and novel technologies in a live environment without "hard cutovers" that risk clinical downtime. 2.2 Governance, XLAs, Enforcement, & Modern Deliverables Problem Statement: Legacy user-facing services suffer from fragmented governance, static administrative reporting, and unregulated product intake. Standard Service Level Agreements (SLAs) lack financial enforcement linked to actual user satisfaction, making it difficult for the Government to hold vendors accountable for real-world mission outcomes. As used in this provision- "Eligible contractor" means a business entity operated on a for-profit or nonprofit basis that- (1) Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than 33 percent of its total workforce over the 12-month period prior to issuance of the solicitation; (2) Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to 29 U.S.C. 206 to the employees who are severely disabled individuals; and (3) Provides, for its employees, health insurance and a retirement plan comparable to those provided for employees by business entities of similar size in its industrial sector or geographic region. "Severely disabled individual" means an individual with a disability (as defined in 42 U.S.C. 12102) who has a severe physical or mental impairment that seriously limits one or more functional capacities.
